in_pashto.name: اسکری

in_pashto.long_meaning: اسکری نوم د عربی ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی، په ځانګړي ډول د 'س-ک-ر' ریښې څخه، چې د پوځ یا لشکر معنی لري. په اسلامي دود کې، دا نوم د پوځي ژوند، زړورتیا، او کنټرول سره تړاو لري. دا نوم ډیری وختونه د هغو کسانو سره تړاو لري چې د پوځي شاليدې څخه راځي یا پوځي ارزښتونو ته ارزښت ورکوي.

It is also a name that is associated with the military and soldiers, emphasizing the role of serving and protecting.

Overall, the name "Askari" highlights the importance of playing a role in the defense and preservation of Islam, both in a physical and spiritual sense.

historical_references.reference: The Askariya (As-Sayyid al-Askari) were a Shia dynasty that ruled the northern parts of Iraq between the 9th and 13th centuries AD. They are named after their founder, the sixth Shia Imam, Ali al-Hadi (828-868 AD), who was also known as Abu al-Abbas al-Askari. The term Askari means 'soldier' or 'soldiery' in Arabic, and the dynasty was so called because of their military protectors.

The Askari shrine in Samarra, Iraq, is the final resting place of the twelfth Shia Imam, Muhammad al-Mahdi, who disappeared in 874 AD and is believed to be in occultation (hidden from the world) and will reappear at the end of time. The Askari shrine is a significant pilgrimage site for Shia Muslims and was a target of destruction by the Mongols in 1258 AD, which led to widespread devastation and loss of life in Iraq.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Askari' in the modern context refers to individuals who serve in the military, security forces, or provide protection and defence in various capacities. This term has its roots in Islamic history and is derived from the Arabic word 'askar' which means 'army' or 'soldier'. In contemporary usage, it is seen on social media platforms where it is used to refer to soldiers and security personnel in a positive light. It is also used in military institutions to refer to personnel and their roles. Within Islamic communities, the term 'Askari' holds a revered status as it is associated with the martyrdom of Husain ibn Ali, the grandson of Prophet Muhammad, at the Battle of Karbala. During the annual commemoration of this event called 'Ashura', the term is used to pay respects to those who have sacrificed their lives in the cause of justice and righteousness.
